findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The Board tab does not meet the requirement that each item show its state in plain words and its next step. This branch's board fixture has a ready row with `pr.checks: "unknown"`; the lookup here gives it no state. An existing client viewed from another machine also has a ready row with `next.step: null` (`tests/test_board_counts.py:219-224`), so the pane shows only its title even though `next.line` names who merges it. The older-board proof likewise expects a bare ready-row title (`tests/test_fix_pane_grouped_board.py:114-117`).
findings.title: Not done: Ready-to-merge rows can omit their state and next step

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. A completed worker round can leave a question in `codex.record` (`src/forge/worker.py:329-334`). The new flag puts that item under Needs you, but the row's `next.step` comes from `_item`, which does not inspect that question and can say `forge close <item>` or `forge work <item>` (`src/forge/nextstep.py:783-870`). This line displays that step as `decide: forge ...`; calling close or work without an answer is refused (`src/forge/close.py:141-143`, `src/forge/worker.py:113-114`). The required action is `forge work <item> --note "<answer>"`.
findings.title: Needs you gives worker questions a command that refuses the answerless call

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The new command-level case creates an unanswered review stop, while the mounted pane case supplies a fabricated resolve step and a ready row with passing checks. Neither checks a real worker question or a ready row with unknown checks or no `next.step`. Those tests pass with both defects above present. The existing worker-question test (`tests/test_machine_views.py:115-129`) checks an occurrence, not the Board tab's state or next step.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Gate. The recorded allowance describes two small fields in board data. The diff also adds `step` to the public `forge next --json` result here, adds `needs_person` to `forge board --json` (`src/forge/board.py:505`), and changes the refresh timeout from 20 to 60 seconds (`src/forge/mod/hooks/register.ts:10`). It therefore changes machine interfaces and refresh behavior beyond the allowance's stated reason.
findings.title: Recorded allowance does not match the interface and timeout changes

stop.proposed: cut the code that invites these findings; or replace the cases with one general rule; or narrow that Done when item; or make it fail closed

why: The pane's Board tab is hard to read: raw timestamps, unknown rounds, zero times, a stage chain that does not mark where an item is, and priority codes
